real_estate.homebuilder: Mortgage rates hit a new one year high of 7.24% as the Fed's quarter point hike took effect today, and mortgage applications fell 4.1%.
real_estate.commentary: 🔔 Mortgage rates hit a new one year high: The Fed's quarter point hike took effect today, putting its target range at 3.75% to 4.00%. Mortgage News Daily's final Wednesday reading put the 30-year fixed at 7.24% and the 15-year at 6.84%, both up 0.02 from Tuesday and the highest readings of the past year. Yesterday's report carried MND's 7.19% morning reading, taken before the announcement. The 10-Year closed Wednesday at 5.01%, its highest close since July 2007, and eased to about 4.95% this morning. At Fremont's median list price of $1,250,000, a 20% down loan is $1,000,000, under Alameda County's $1,249,125 high-balance conforming limit. At 7.24%, principal and interest run about $6,815 a month, $34 more than at Wednesday morning's 7.19%, and every eighth of a point is about $85. Buyers are pausing. The Mortgage Bankers Association says applications fell 4.1% in the week ending September 11, with purchase applications down 1% and refinances down 9%. Refinances are 65% below a year ago, and MBA's 30-year average reached 6.97%, its highest since May 2025. The newsletter called that average "over 7%"; MBA's own survey is just under it, while MND's daily index is above. For more on what the hike means for Bay Area buyers and sellers, including the next Fed meeting dates, read the full write up on Harv's blog: What the Fed hike means for Bay Area buyers and sellers 📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus) • Board wide: 2,730 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 203 coming soon and 195 brand new. • Five city ledger: 708 live listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 615 are already on the market and 93 are coming soon. • Fremont: 258 live, 202 active, 43 coming soon, 13 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,250,000 at $805 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 29 days. • The rest of the ledger: Hayward 181, Milpitas 120, Newark 88, Union City 61. • Across all five cities the median is $1,099,000 at $687 a square foot. 272 homes are priced under a million, and 158 have been sitting 60 days or longer. What this means for you: the ledger ticked up to 708 from 706, Union City added five listings, and homes sitting 60 days or more fell to 158 from 167. Buyers: with fewer people applying for loans, the line at the open house may be shorter, so refresh your approval at today's rates before you write. Sellers: the buyers still shopping are pricing in 7%, so price for today's rates, not last spring's.

feature_images.alt: Step chart of the Federal Reserve's target range from 2022 to 2026: hikes to 5.25% to 5.50% by July 2023, cuts from September 2024 to December 2025 down to 3.50% to 3.75%, and the September 16, 2026 increase to 3.75% to 4.00%, with a box listing the hike odds of 85.6%, 92.3% and 92.7% reported beforehand.
feature_images.caption: The Fed's quarter point increase to 3.75% to 4.00%, its first since July 2023, took effect today.

stocks.note: Levels are Wednesday, September 16 at the closing bell. Thursday is live: at 8:45 AM PT the S&P was 7,634.67 (+1.10%), the Dow 51,794.34 (+0.65%) and the Nasdaq 26,399.18 (+1.62%).
stocks.news:
Stocks slipped on Fed day Wednesday, with the Dow off 1.21% and the Nasdaq about flat, then bounced Thursday morning, led by the Nasdaq. Weekly jobless claims came in at 196,000 for the week ending September 12, down 10,000, so the job market is still holding up.

J.B. Hunt fell 13.30% Wednesday after the trucking company warned its third quarter earnings will drop 5% to 10% from the second quarter, citing higher fuel and driver costs. Generac jumped after the bell on a deal to supply backup generators for Amazon's data centers that also gives Amazon the right to buy up to $340 million of Generac stock. It traded near $249 late Wednesday and about $209 this morning, still up about 19%.

economy.note: All four are Wednesday, September 16. The 10-Year is the Treasury daily yield curve close, gold and silver are the COMEX front month at Wednesday's 1:00 PM PT print measured against Tuesday's same time print, and Brent is the ICE front month settlement. Thursday so far: at 8:35 AM PT gold was $4,399.60, silver $66.30, and Brent was trading near $103.59, a live tick, not a settlement.
economy.commentary:
The Fed's new target range of 3.75% to 4.00% is now in effect. Its next two meetings are October 27 to 28 and December 8 to 9, and the Fed's own projections from Wednesday point to one more quarter point increase this year.

The 10-Year closed Wednesday at 5.01%, up 0.01 and its highest close since July 2007, then eased to about 4.95% this morning. The Labor Department's weekly report showed 196,000 new unemployment claims, 10,000 fewer than the week before.

Oil and metals: Brent settled at $105.83 Wednesday, down 2.69%, and was near $103.59 this morning. At Wednesday's 1:00 PM PT print, gold fell 0.71% to $4,302.50 and silver fell 1.19% to $63.42. Both bounced overnight, with gold at $4,399.60 and silver at $66.30 as of 8:35 AM PT.

A note on the newsletter's numbers: its stocks and mortgage rates check out. It had the 10-Year at 4.99%, down 0.01, but Treasury shows a 5.01% close, up 0.01. It had Brent up 0.08% at $105.91, but the settlement was $105.83, down 2.69%. It had gold at $4,347, down 0.90%, but the 1:00 PM PT print was $4,302.50, down 0.71%. Silver was left out again.

crypto.commentary:
Live quotes pulled at 8:45 AM PT with 24 hour changes. All three are higher this morning, led by Ether, up about 3%.

Wednesday was quieter. After Tuesday's stalled Senate vote on the Clarity Act, Bitcoin stayed between about $75,600 and $76,150 through Wednesday afternoon, Fed decision included.

A note on the newsletter: it showed small gains for all three as of 4:00 PM ET Wednesday. Against Tuesday at the same hour, Bitcoin was down 0.14% and Ether 0.33%, while XRP was up 0.36%.
